prompt.name: log-workflow-history

context.source: The local conversation history of this session: the developer's prompts and your answers.

prompt.outcome: Record the session's prompt history in the workflow log by following the template that is already in the log file. Add one row to the "Role Decisions" table for each developer prompt, in chronological order.

steps.step: Read the target file first and follow its existing template and any instructions written in it.
For each developer prompt, add one table row with these columns: Time, Role, Exact prompt used, Result reviewed, Developer decision, Next action.
Fill "Time" with the date and time of the prompt. Use the real current time (for example from `date`), and never invent one.
Fill "Role" with the role that was active for that prompt.
Fill "Exact prompt used" with the developer's prompt preserved word for word. For a long pasted prompt, give a faithful summary and say it is a summary.
Fill "Result reviewed" with a short description of the artifact or answer that came back. Never copy the full response.
Fill "Developer decision" with accept, clarify or correct, based on what the developer did next.
Fill "Next action" with the role or action the developer selected next. If none has been chosen yet, say so.
Add the rows by editing the existing table. Keep every existing row and every other section unchanged.

constraints.constraint: Omit the prompt that requests the logging itself, and any other prompt the developer asks to omit. If only part of a prompt is to be omitted, say so in its row.
Do not fill the Task id, Developer, start and finish timestamps, runtime readiness, browser observation, completion or known limitations fields unless the developer asks for it.
Do not invent results, decisions or timestamps. If something is unknown, write that it is unknown.
Do not change any other file.

prompt.report: Reply with a short summary of which rows were added. State anything you summarised instead of copying, and any cell you filled in yourself, so the developer can correct it.
